validated_results.title: Association of Cigarette Smoking and Alcohol Drinking With Risk of 12 Common Cancers Among Low-Income American Adults in the Southeastern United States.
validated_results.journal: Cancer control : journal of the Moffitt Cancer Center
validated_results.reason: This prospective cohort study evaluated alcohol consumption and incident prostate cancer risk among 74,286 adults in the Southern Community Cohort Study, though numerical risk estimates for prostate cancer were provided in supplementary tables.

design.excerpt: The SCCS is an ongoing prospective cohort study, with the aim to investigate risk factors of chronic diseases and health disparities between Black and White adults in a low-income, low-education population across 12 southeastern U.S. states
design.location: Methods, Study Participants and Data Collection, paragraph 1

timing.excerpt: We prospectively investigated the associations between cigarette smoking, alcohol drinking, and the risk of twelve cancer types among over 74 000 low-income Black and White adults from the Southern Community Cohort Study in the United States.

continent.excerpt: across 12 southeastern U.S. states: Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia, and West Virginia
